Lesson §1.2 tầng 7 / §10 set oxygen targets 'SpO2 ≥ 90–92%' and §10 'mục tiêu ≥ 92–94%'; AAP 2014 uses 90% — item A08/A14 use SpO2 87–88% to stay unambiguous; target value not tested.

Lesson §7 Bẫy 6/§9 Checkpoint 1 claims infants < 6 months have few β2 receptors/immature airway smooth muscle and that corticoids prolong viral shedding — not mainstream-verified; not tested (A09 tests only 'mucus plugging/edema, not smooth-muscle spasm').

Lesson §7 Bẫy 1 / §8 Pearl 10 / §9 Checkpoint 3 claim atelectasis has NO air bronchogram and air bronchogram 'excludes' obstructive atelectasis 100% — distal (bronchiolar) atelectasis can show air bronchograms; A07 tests only volume loss (fissure/diaphragm shift) not air bronchogram.
Lesson §1.2 tầng 5 gives a vagal mechanism for RSV apnea; mechanism not agreed in references — A11 tests only the clinical fact (apnea risk in neonates/preterm).

Lesson §4.4 claims RSV+hMPV co-infection raises PICU ventilation risk 2–3x via TLR-4/TLR-7/8 cytokine storm; literature is conflicting (early studies suggested higher severity, later ones did not) — not tested; A17 only tests multiplex PCR to look for co-pathogens.

Lesson §4.3 age peaks (RSV 2–6 months vs hMPV 6 months–2 years) and 'higher fever in hMPV than RSV' are soft epidemiologic tendencies; hMPV and rhinovirus also cannot be separated clinically. A18 is restricted to the five lesson pathogens and offers a combined-clue stem (age, RSV-negative test, no adeno/pneumococcus/Mycoplasma clues); rated difficulty 3.
Lesson §4.3: 'hMPV is one of the leading triggers of severe asthma attacks'; in mainstream sources rhinovirus is the leading trigger — A19 tests management (treat as asthma) not 'leading trigger'.

Lesson has no RSV prevention content; A10 (palivizumab for ex-28-week BPD infant) is based on AAP 2014 palivizumab criteria; nirsevimab/maternal RSVpreF are newer options deliberately not offered as distractors/keys.
Lesson §0.3 'Mycoplasma 30–50% of school-age CAP' and §0.1 percentages (60–70% of visits; 70–80% viral) not tested as numbers.

Lesson §3.2 tầng 7 gives Doxycycline only for children ≥ 8 years and Levofloxacin/Moxifloxacin for < 8 years or severe disease; AAP Red Book allows short-course doxycycline at any age and treats fluoroquinolones as last-line. Only the ≥ 8-year doxycycline case was tested (B12); no < 8-year regimen item written.

Lesson §8 Pearl 3 calls Adenovirus (esp. serotype 7) 'căn nguyên số 1' of fever > 7 days with the PCF triad; mainstream references describe pharyngoconjunctival fever as usually self-limited and mostly serotypes 3, 4, 7 — claim of 'No. 1 cause' not tested; items use the triad only as a clue.

Lesson claims CRP 80–150 mg/L and WBC > 20,000 as the Adenovirus 'trap' and Procalcitonin rising like sepsis; PCT behaviour is variable in references, so PCT is used only as a non-discriminating distractor (B06), not as a key.

Lesson §3.1 calls Mycoplasma 'kháng tự nhiên 100%' to beta-lactams, 'tuyệt đối không thấy vi khuẩn' on Gram stain, and a 'màng lipid ba lớp'; absolute wording and the 3-layer membrane statement not tested verbatim (Mycoplasma simply stains poorly/not at all).
Lesson dose 'Azithromycin 10 mg/kg/ngày x 5 ngày' differs from the common regimen (10 mg/kg day 1, then 5 mg/kg days 2–5); doses were not tested.
Lesson reports cold agglutinins in 50–60% of patients and that MIRM was formerly mislabeled SJS; prevalence figures not tested, only the mechanism (B18).

Lesson describes Swyer-James-MacLeod as 'viêm tắc mao mạch phổi mạn tính'; mainstream treats it as a unilateral form of post-infectious bronchiolitis obliterans. Item B08 tests only the radiologic picture (hyperlucent, small lung, sparse vessels) which both sources agree on.
B19: serology (single IgM) is a plausible partial-credit distractor in Vietnamese practice; key chosen per IDSA/AAP preference for NAAT early in illness.

Lesson §8 Pearl 10 ('air bronchogram khẳng định 100% tổn thương phế nang, loại trừ xẹp phổi') overstates: air bronchogram can also occur in some non-obstructive/passive atelectasis — C06/C14 test only the mechanism and the volume-loss sign, not the absolute claim.

Lesson §8 Pearl 5 / §7 Bẫy 8 present grunting as a 'phế cầu red flag'; grunting is a nonspecific sign of severe lower respiratory disease in any pathogen — used only as a severity cue in C03/C07, never as pathogen-specific discriminator.

§5.2 day ranges of the four stages (ngày 2–4, 4–8, >8) are textbook approximations and rarely seen classically in the antibiotic era — used only for ordering; C03/C04 stems also include pathology/physical-sign clues.

§4.4 / §7 Bẫy 5 claim RSV+hMPV co-infection raises PICU/ventilation risk 2–3× and recommends multiplex PCR in non-responders: evidence is mixed and AAP 2014 does not recommend routine viral testing — not tested.

§4.4 claim that rapid antigen tests cannot detect hMPV is not universally true (rapid hMPV antigen assays exist in some settings) — only the multiplex PCR confirming hMPV is used (C11/C18), without asserting rapid tests fail.
§6 lists Mycoplasma age 5–15 y and doxycycline only ≥8 y; Mycoplasma also occurs in <5 y and AAP Red Book allows short doxycycline courses at any age — doxycycline age cut-off not tested.
§7 Bẫy 6 claims systemic corticoid prolongs viral shedding in RSV; mainstream evidence is simply 'no benefit' — not tested.

§2.1 / C17: adenovirus resistance to alcohol is relative (non-enveloped viruses are less susceptible to alcohol hand rubs, need prolonged contact or hypochlorite); stem says only that alcohol wiping failed to stop spread.

§5.3 high-dose amoxicillin 80–90 mg/kg/day matches PIDS/IDSA (90 mg/kg/day in 2 doses); IDSA prefers ampicillin/penicillin G IV for hospitalised fully-immunised children, ceftriaxone/cefotaxime when not immunised or high local resistance — C07 therefore asks only 'kháng sinh tiêm tĩnh mạch' without naming the drug.
